title: Gerald Lascelles's Beaulieu festival and first solo trips to Britain
summary: Invited to a British festival, Freeman played with Chris Barber, then arranged solo tours with the Alex Welch band, coming two or three times yearly.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Then I started to go to Europe. I got -- let's see, George Wein gave a party -- George Wein had now moved into New York and in his apartment he gave a party for Gerald Lascelles, the Queen's cousin, and he invited me to the party and I met Gerald Lascelles, and he was all over me, we were very good friends and he said, 'Oh, I have been following your records, ever since I was a young man,' and he said, 'We are going to have a big jazz festival -- now, this was about 16 years ago, we're going to have a big jazz festival in Beulay, outside of Manchester and I would like you to come. I have invited you, Buck Clayton and Dizzy Gillespie,' so we went over and we worked in three different bands.
Dizzy was with Johnny Dankworth and Buck was with Humphrey Littleton and I worked with Chris Barber, and Alex

Welch, it seems to me was on that thing. I didn't work with him but I met him and a year later, I -- oh, no, after I got back about a month later I wrote -- Harold Davidson had come backstage, that's right, and I told him I would like to work there as a soloist, so I sent him a letter and he sent back a very nice letter saying that I should get in touch with his man, Jack Higgins, which I did and so told Higgins I wanted to come over and work with the Alex Welch band as a soloist.
So that caught on and I was coming --
Why do you think that was.
That was -- I'd say that the first time -- well, I came here 16 years ago and this is now -- we're almost into -- '62, yes, you said that. Let's see if that's right. Yes, it has to be '62.
Now, I was coming over two and three times a year, we see. We were because it was very successful, doing a lot of business with the band.
